candidateEvidence.excerpt: OpenAI released a Data agent in ChatGPT Work on September 10. It is a workplace data tool that can connect an approved account to company data, investigate a question and build a dashboard. A colleague can ask why sales slowed without first writing a database query.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: OpenAI dated the release September 10, 2026 and introduced the Data agent in ChatGPT Work. OpenAI says it connects to approved sources including Amazon Redshift, Datadog, Google BigQuery, ClickHouse, Databricks, MongoDB and Snowflake, and can also use files and documents from Google Drive and SharePoint. OpenAI says it uses an organization's business terms, metric definitions, custom calculations and data relationships from semantic layers and trusted sources to interpret data. OpenAI says enterprise administrators choose which data connections and roles are available, while queries enforce the connected account's existing table, row and column permissions. OpenAI says users can ask follow-up questions and review the evidence behind findings, then build, edit, share and refresh interactive dashboards. OpenAI says the agent can recommend next steps, share findings through Slack or email, and carry out actions the user approves through connected tools. OpenAI says the Data plugin appears in the Plugins directory in ChatGPT Work; administrators can install it, configure relevant data-source plugins and manage who can use them.

Primary for the September 10 release, product scope, connections, permissions, workflow and availability claims. Limitation: Feature, internal-adoption and customer-result descriptions are vendor claims. The release supplies no public accuracy benchmark and no new standalone price.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: The largest evidence gap is accuracy. VentureBeat asked OpenAI for a retrieval or correctness benchmark for the external product and reported that none has been published. OpenAI described an internal comparison with its own data tools but supplied no public number. There is no independent hands-on benchmark yet showing how reliably it answers questions across customers' systems.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: VentureBeat reported on September 10 that the Data agent connects to enterprise data sources and turns findings into dashboards, recommendations and follow-up actions. OpenAI told VentureBeat that the product stitches existing context together at use time rather than creating a new persistent context layer. VentureBeat reported that OpenAI has not published a retrieval-accuracy or correctness benchmark for the external Data agent product. The report says OpenAI described an internal comparison against its own data tools but did not provide a published number; VentureBeat characterized that as an internal comparison rather than an independently verified benchmark. VentureBeat concluded that the shift does not remove the need for data engineering because access controls and audit trails still need maintenance.

Independent reporting based on an interview with OpenAI's enterprise technology lead; primary for what the reporter asked and what OpenAI disclosed about external evaluation. Limitation: The article is reporting and analysis, not a hands-on evaluation of Data agent outputs or an independent product benchmark.

scopeAndFreshness: VentureBeat excerpt states no retrieval-accuracy or correctness benchmark has been published for the external product; article retains VentureBeat attribution.
